title: Google fixes Chrome Gemini memory issue: a single tab once ate up 8.4GB, and even logged-out sessions could climb to 1.3GB

content_html:
The culprit that turns your browser into a slideshow isn’t always web ads—sometimes it’s the AI chat window itself. According to tech media outlet Android Headline on November 26, Google has fixed the issue of the Gemini web app using excessively high memory in Chrome for long periods—the response didn’t come early; user complaints had been piling up on two platforms for a long time: Reddit and the Chromium issue tracker, where multiple people reported Gemini tabs using up to 6.4GB of memory, with peaks at 8.4GB.

How the memory usage climbed

The issue tracker contains a clear data trail. A December 2025 Chromium report showed that a logged-out Gemini session could see memory usage climb from 100MB all the way to 1.3GB, while the number of page elements ballooned to 85,621 at the same time; other users found that even a short conversation with just 5 messages and an attached PDF could see memory rise from 250MB to 900MB within 15 minutes. For everyday users, the consequences are very real: using Gemini in Chrome for a long time to look up information, write, or do research makes the computer noticeably sluggish, and other tabs and apps are affected as well.

The fix is live, no manual update needed

The Google support team gave a brief response on Reddit: the fix has been rolled out, and users don’t need to manually install an update or change settings—they can just use it as usual. The company also left the door open—if abnormal memory usage occurs again during future use, users are welcome to keep reporting it to them. A tab that devoured 8.4GB has now taken its final bow, though how much memory the fix actually saves will have to wait for real-world user data to tell.
